source: https://aci.aero/resources/busiest-airports-in-the-world/ (ACI World Airport Traffic Dataset 2026); final release https://aci.aero/2026/07/15/worlds-busiest-airports-atlanta-holds-asia-climbs-strong-demand-while-asia-pacific-growth-reshape-the-rankings/; preliminary https://aci.aero/2026/04/14/worlds-busiest-airports-revealed-in-latest-global-rankings/
published: 2026-07-15 (final total-passenger ranking); preliminary 2026-04-14; resources page shows the international top 20 and states the dataset was published September 2026

US.basis: Busiest US airport by international passengers in 2025 (over 34 million international passengers), ahead of MIA, LAX, SFO, EWR
US.source: https://simpleflying.com/7-busiest-airports-us-international-passenger-traffic/ (secondary; underlying figures from Port Authority of NY & NJ / US DOT)

BR.basis: Brazil's largest international hub, 47.1M total passengers in 2025; CGH (Congonhas) handles domestic flights only

JP.basis: Largest share of Japan's international passengers in 2025: Narita 29.7%, Kansai 24.0%, Haneda 21.3% (of a record 114.4M). ACI 2025 international ranking lists NRT at 35.0M; HND is not in the international top 20

CA.basis: Toronto Pearson is Canada's busiest airport and largest international gateway; no 2025 international figure fetched this session

AU.basis: Sydney is Australia's largest international airport; BITRE publishes airport-level international data but the airport shares were not retrieved this session

MX.basis: By international passengers Cancun led Mexico in 2025 with 19.56M (-3.6%) ahead of Mexico City AICM with 17.48M (+2.1%). MEX leads on total passengers (44.6M) and is the capital's gateway, but not the country's top international airport

KR.basis: ACI 2025 international rank 3, 73,554,772 international passengers; GMP is mainly domestic

FR.basis: ACI 2025 international rank 7, 66,135,938; ORY not in the international top 20

IE.basis: Dublin handles the large majority of Ireland's international traffic (Cork and Shannon far smaller); no figure fetched this session

IS.basis: Keflavik is Iceland's international airport; Reykjavik (RKV) is domestic plus limited Greenland/Faroes service; no figure fetched this session

NZ.basis: Auckland is New Zealand's largest international airport; no figure fetched this session

LV.basis: Riga is Latvia's only airport with significant scheduled international service; no figure fetched this session

uncertain: Year given is 2025 (ACI published it in 2026), per the instruction to prefer the 2025 ranking; the 2024 ranking was not collected.

ACI's April 2026 preliminary blog figures differ slightly from the July 2026 final release (PVG 84,994,227 vs 84,994,548; ORD 84,814,099 vs 84,856,018; HKG international 60,824,359 vs 60,810,724). The final/resources-page figures are used.
The international top 20 was read from ACI's resources page, which says the dataset was published September 2026; the exact date of that page was not confirmed.
Airport full names in 'name' were added from general knowledge; ACI lists city, country code and IATA code only.
Mexico: the brief assumed MEX, but CUN has more international passengers (2025: 19.56M vs 17.48M). Choose MEX if 'gateway' means the capital's airport rather than the top by international passengers.
US: JFK figure comes from a secondary source (Simple Flying), not directly from DOT or PANYNJ.
CA, AU, IE, IS, NZ, LV gateways are well established but were not checked against a fetched 2025 statistic this session; source is null (or a figure was not extracted) for those.
